title: Event-Driven Development with Azure Functions
description: Design event-driven architectures using Azure Functions, Event Grid, and Event Hub for loosely coupled systems.

data.text: Event-driven architecture means your system reacts to events—things that have happened—rather than waiting for requests. Azure Functions is a natural fit for this pattern because it is built around triggers.
In an event-driven system, producers emit events without knowing who will consume them. Consumers (functions) react to events independently.
Azure Event Grid is a fully managed event routing service. It delivers events from Azure services (Blob Storage, Resource Groups, etc.) to subscribers like Azure Functions.

data.title: Bicep — Event Grid Trigger with Storage Event

data.text: For high-throughput streaming scenarios, use Event Hub triggers. Event Hub ingests millions of events per second, and Azure Functions can process them in parallel.

data.title: C# — Event Hub Trigger
Fan-Out Pattern
data.text: Use multiple functions listening to the same queue or Event Hub to scale processing horizontally. Each function instance processes events independently, increasing throughput automatically.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Event-driven systems react to events rather than requests
Event Grid routes events from Azure services to Functions
Multiple consumers can process the same events independently
data.takeaway: Event-driven Functions enable loosely coupled, scalable architectures.
